name: MD-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Hoyer's retirement keeps seat in Democratic hands via strong primary winner
Adrian Boafo heavily funded with $12M outside support and no opposition spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: This Maryland seat carries a D+17 partisan lean and the Democratic nominee, Adrian Boafo, enters the general with strong fundraising and roughly $12 million in outside support against no visible opposition spending. Prediction markets price a Democratic win around 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for the Republican nominee or an unusually strong national Republican environment could narrow the margin, though a seat this blue is very unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Steny Hoyer (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Steny Hoyer's retirement opens a deep-blue Maryland seat that has long favored Democrats by wide margins. The district's partisan lean of D+17 makes a Republican takeover a steep climb under any plausible national environment. Adrian Boafo emerged from the Democratic primary with a strong fundraising record and benefits from roughly $12 million in outside support, while no outside money is opposing him.

Republican Chris Chaffee has reported little in the way of fundraising or cash on hand, leaving him badly outmatched financially. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96%, and the seat's fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the low twenties. The race is rated Safe D.
